learning_outcomes.title: Solving with similar triangles
learning_outcomes.statement: Use similar triangles to solve problems.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: Establish similarity by AA, SAS, or SSS. Write corresponding vertices in order, set up a proportion, and solve. Check that all lengths use the same units.

questions.title: A • Nested triangles
questions.stem: In triangle ABC, D lies on AB and E lies on AC. DE ∥ BC. AD = 6, DB = 4, AE = 9, and BC = 15.

parts.prompt: Prove that triangle ADE is similar to triangle ABC.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: ∠DAE=∠BAC (common angle), and ∠ADE=∠ABC (corresponding angles with DE∥BC). Thus ADE~ABC by AA. Award 3.
AB=6+4=10, so the scale factor is AD/AB=6/10=3/5. Award 1.

parts.prompt: Find AC and EC, showing a proportion.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: 9/AC=3/5 gives AC=15. Therefore EC=15−9=6. Award 2 for proportion/AC and 1 for EC.

parts.prompt: Find DE and the ratio of the two triangle areas.

questions.title: B • Shadows and unit conversion
questions.stem: A vertical 1.5 m measuring pole casts a 0.75 m shadow. At the same moment, a nearby vertical tower casts a shadow 18 m long on the same level ground.

parts.prompt: Sketch and label the two triangles. Explain why they are similar.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: Two right triangles have equal sun-elevation angles, so they are similar by AA. Award 1 for labeled sketch and 2 for justification.

parts.prompt: Write and solve a proportion for the tower height.
A second pole is 180 cm tall. Predict its shadow length in metres at the same moment.
State two physical assumptions that support this model.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: Examples include level ground, vertical poles/tower, simultaneous measurements, and parallel sunlight. Award 1 for each of two valid assumptions.

questions.title: C • SSS and SAS reasoning
questions.stem: Triangle ABC has AB = 6, AC = 9, BC = 12. Triangle DEF has DE = 10, DF = 15, EF = 20.

parts.prompt: Use SSS to prove the triangles similar and write a correct similarity statement.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: AB/DE=6/10=3/5, AC/DF=9/15=3/5, BC/EF=12/20=3/5. Thus ABC~DEF by SSS. Award 3.

parts.prompt: In a separate pair of similar triangles with the same small-to-large scale factor 3:5, the smaller median is 7.2. Find the corresponding larger median.
In a separate pair, XY = 8, XZ = 12, PQ = 10, PR = 15, and ∠X = ∠P = 40°. Prove XYZ ~ PQR.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: XY/PQ=8/10=4/5 and XZ/PR=12/15=4/5. The included angles X and P are congruent, so XYZ~PQR by SAS. Award 3.

parts.prompt: Explain why matching only one angle in the separate pair would be insufficient.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: A single angle can occur in many triangles with different other angles and side ratios. Another valid criterion is needed. Award 2.

import_notes.original_text: A median from A has length 7.2. Find the corresponding median from D.
import_notes.revised_text: In a separate pair of similar triangles with the same small-to-large scale factor 3:5, the smaller median is 7.2. Find the corresponding larger median.
import_notes.reason: The sides 6, 9, 12 in part (a) imply a median from A of sqrt(90)/2, not 7.2. A separate pair preserves the intended proportionality exercise and answer 12.
